The number in parentheses (3H, 2H, 1H, 4H) tells us how many hydrogens are in each equivalent set, but the question asks for the number of different types (environments), not the total number of hydrogens.

Therefore, there are 4 different types of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms in this compound.
